description:
Code, certificates and logs for the paper of the same title, together with the paper itself: the programs, certificates and logs of its computer-assisted proofs.

Abstract. With computer-assisted proofs that ℂ6 admits at most three mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) now available, ℂ10 is the smallest dimension in which it is unknown whether a complete set of d+1=11 MUBs exists; only three MUBs are known. We prove that every triple of mutually unbiased product bases of ℂ2⊗ℂ5 is strongly unextendible: no vector is unbiased to all three bases. Consequently no set of four MUBs in dimension ten, and in particular no complete set, contains three product bases. This settles the case d=2×5 anticipated by McNulty, Pammer and Weigert; it was known only for the Heisenberg–Weyl triple. The proof covers all ten equivalence classes with explicit Nullstellensatz certificates modulo one prime on 91 charts of ℙ9×ℙ9 for each class (910 in all), transferred to characteristic zero by a projective reduction lemma, together with an independent rank certificate for eight of the ten classes. We also prove that the pair formed by the standard and the Fourier basis of ℂ10 is contained in no set of four MUBs. Exactly 3040 rays are unbiased to both bases (this confirms the count found numerically by Führ and Rzeszotnik), each of them is unbiased to at most eight of the others, and every triple formed by the pair and a third MUB is strongly unextendible. For this we certify 34,940 cyclic 10-roots in Krawczyk uniqueness boxes, decide unimodularity exactly through an involution, and prove completeness by a four-dimensional interval branch-and-bound obtained from the Chinese-remainder splitting ℤ10=ℤ2×ℤ5.

Contents. paper/: LaTeX source and PDF of the paper. scripts/: all programs (generation, certification, verification). logs/: logs of the reference verification runs; logs/bb/ has all 256 branch-and-bound subproblems and the final merge. data/: the 0.6 GB certificate archive (910 chart systems with cofactor certificates, eight rank witnesses, approximate cyclic-10 roots, certified ray data), split into 90 MB parts, with SHA-256 lists; reassembly and verification commands are in README.md.
